cells.tense: Right now you're tending it — both of them, in the same pair of hands.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing with steady, responsible care.
cells.place: In the not-knowing, where you can only see as far as the next step.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've been holding finish, and let the finish be enough — offer the completion to be seen by someone, and let the release come on its own. What comes back is a weight that lifts without being pushed.
cells.core: You're tending what's growing — both of them — and you're not forcing either one. You don't need the whole road to take the next step, and that's exactly how you're doing it. The care is steady and it costs you something, and it's working.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing without forcing it, one step at a time.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead is the version where everything is finally handled, and you're already living in it.
cells.verb: Tending harder than the thing asked, ahead of its own timing.
cells.place: In the fog, where you keep trying to map the whole road before you'll take the first step.
cells.ask: Let one piece of what you're imagining be finished before you go back to worrying it — offer the abundance already realized, and let satisfaction come from experience that's been fully felt. What comes back is a care that doesn't exhaust.
cells.core: You're carrying both loads and a third one nobody handed you, and you're already bracing for the part that isn't here yet. The tending has turned into clutching — you can't put it down long enough to see what's actually growing. The care is real. The grip on it is costing you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it all before it's even here, and the grip is tiring you out.

cells.tense: Somewhere back there, you stopped tending it, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.verb: Tending that withdrew when it wasn't safe to keep going.
cells.place: In the fog, where you've stopped trusting the step to reveal the next.
cells.ask: Put your hope on one thing still growing, however small, and keep following it after everything — offer the persistence that comes from aspiration, and let what you cultivate shine once it's finished. What comes back is a care that doesn't exhaust.
cells.core: You stopped tending it. Not because you didn't care — because at some point the caring ran dry, and you stepped back, and the fog got thicker. The capacity is still there. It's just not being fed, and you're not sure the next step is worth taking.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending it, and the fog filled the space where the care was.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but the room is still being written.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, while calling it something that happens on its own.
cells.place: In ambiguity you're already moving through — you just haven't called it navigating.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you've been tending is yours — offer the intent to be seen by someone who can honor it, and let the release come from finishing rather than defeat. What comes back is a care that doesn't exhaust.
cells.core: You've been tending something for a while — patiently, with real care, in the fog — and describing it as just what the situation needed. The stewarding is already running. What's missing is your name on it, to yourself most of all.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending it. You've been calling it just what the situation needed.
